results.controlIntent: a. Use internal system clocks to produce time stamps for audit records; and b. Record, for audit records, those time stamps meeting [Assignment: organization-defined granularity of time measurement] that satisfy one or more of the following: use Coordinated Universal Time; have a fixed local time offset from Coordinated Universal Time; include the local time offset as part of the time stamp.

judgment.rationale: Both CloudTrail audit records retrieved for the churn-predictor-endpoint (CreateEndpoint and UpdateEndpoint events) carry ISO 8601 timestamps with second-level granularity and an explicit UTC indicator ('Z' suffix). This satisfies AU-8.r3(a) — AWS CloudTrail uses internal system clocks synchronized via AWS Time Sync Service (NTP-backed) to produce these timestamps — and AU-8.r3(b) — the timestamps are expressed in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), meeting the requirement that timestamps use UTC or include an unambiguous time offset. No local-time or offset-ambiguous timestamps were observed. The timestamp format is consistent across all retrieved audit events.
gaps: Organization-defined granularity requirement (e.g., millisecond vs. second precision) was not explicitly documented — current evidence shows second-level granularity only. If the organization mandates sub-second precision, additional verification would be needed.

No direct evidence of the NTP/time-sync configuration for the underlying AWS infrastructure was retrieved; conformance of AU-8.r3(a) relies on AWS's well-known use of its internal Time Sync Service, which may require human attestation or AWS compliance documentation (e.g., SOC 2 report) for formal audit purposes.
